headline: Aerobic base is deepening through the volume ramp, with easy-run HR settled low and time-in-zone almost entirely aerobic.
confidence_reasons: Multiple data sources active in last 3 days
summary:
The picture is clean right now: you've held a near-doubled running block while easy-effort heart rate has settled lower on comparable runs, and the grey-zone share is essentially nil. That combination — more volume, lower cost, disciplined intensity distribution — is exactly the aerobic durability signal you want with a long self-supported effort roughly a month out. This isn't a one-off; it's the third block showing it, so treat it as confirmed rather than provisional.

Strength frequency has held flat across the ramp rather than being sacrificed to running load, which matters more than usual given the pack-carry demands ahead. Keeping that steady while volume climbs is the harder thing to protect, and so far you've done it.

Nothing in today's data pushes toward more caution or a change of direction — the trend is consolidating in a good place. The main open question is durability under load rather than aerobic economy, which the numbers already speak to well.
watch_items: Watch whether easy paces start drifting quicker at the same low HR — that would firm up the economy gain beyond the HR drop alone.
Note how back-to-back and longer efforts feel with a loaded pack, since that specific demand isn't yet reflected in recent runs.
Keep an eye on strength holding through the pre-event weeks as running volume stays elevated.
As more sleep nights accumulate, watch for any pattern between low-score nights and next-day aerobic HR.

evidence_items.text: ▲ 4-week volume 177 km vs 92 km prior block (+92%)
▼ Easy-run HR averaging 142 bpm vs 155 bpm prior period (comparable-effort runs, 9 vs 6 runs)
▲ Zone 2: 211 min vs 180-240 min/week target (117% of minimum); grey zone (Z3+Z4): 0.3%
